proposedchanges.title: Trump Orders Guantánamo Preparation for a 30,000-Person Migrant Detention Capacity
proposedchanges.description_long: President Donald Trump announced on January 30, 2025, that the government would prepare Guantánamo Bay Naval Base to hold up to 30,000 migrants. He said the site would be used for people the administration could not return to their home countries and directed the Department of Homeland Security and Pentagon to expand the existing Migrant Operations Center. Guantánamo is associated with post-September 11 detention of terrorism suspects, while its migrant center had separately been used for immigration cases. The announcement raised questions about conditions and legal protections at a remote military site. The stated capacity was a plan, not an operating population. The supplied reports document the preparation order and announcement; they do not establish that the facility reached 30,000 beds or how long it operated.

evidencebasis: The packet and merged descriptions identify the January 30 announcement, direction to DHS and the Pentagon, and proposed 30,000-person capacity. The description distinguishes the plan from an operating population. The source URLs supplied with the record remain present.
notes: Keep the immigration category. Remove the unsourced later-implementation aside and the internal reference to the entry.

notes: The medium already distinguishes the offer from a completed deal. Replace the unsupported title claim and remove internal audit phrasing from the long.

proposedchanges.title: SEC and Binance Ask Court to Pause Civil Lawsuit for 60 Days
proposedchanges.description_long: On February 10, 2025, Binance and the Securities and Exchange Commission jointly asked a federal court to pause the agency’s civil lawsuit against the exchange for 60 days. The SEC said its new cryptocurrency task force could affect the case and help the parties reach a resolution. The filing was a procedural request, not a court decision, dismissal, or finding about Binance. The supplied account does not report whether the judge granted the pause or what terms the parties discussed. The case remained pending while the agency considered how its new task force might affect the litigation.

evidencebasis: The packet and merged descriptions identify the February 10 joint stay request, its 60-day duration, the SEC’s explanation about its new crypto task force, and the absence of a reported court decision. Both source URLs remain present.
notes: Keep Binance and the SEC as organization tags and retain the event-specific topic tags. Remove the criminal characterization, unrelated corruption category, and unsupported Trump people tag.
